title: Org Vet
description: Authenticate an organization at an explicit level of assurance. The credential is issued to an AID the organization controls, so the organization can authenticate itself by presenting it.

t.description: Message type. Optional; an ACDC JSON message without it is of type acm.

u.description: Salty nonce that blinds this credential's SAID. Optional, but ordinarily wanted: the attested content is a short list of public identifiers and a number between 1 and 4, so an observer who can guess it could otherwise confirm the guess against the SAID this credential's registry publishes.

rd.description: SAID of the registry whose TEL carries this credential's issuance and revocation. Required: an assurance level speaks to a state of affairs that can change, so a vet nobody can withdraw is worse than no vet at all.

u.description: Salty nonce that blinds this block against confirmation by recomputation

i.description: Issuee: the AID controlled by the organization being vetted. Required, because a vet of nobody in particular cannot be presented by the organization it vets.

dt.description: When the vetting was asserted, as an ISO-8601 datetime. The level of assurance speaks as of this moment and not after it.

loa.description: Level of assurance: which verification procedures the issuer performed, where larger means more. Integers 1 (bronze), 2 (silver), 3 (gold) and 4 (platinum) are defined in this credential's documentation; a fractional value expresses a nuance within a tier (2.1 < 2.2), so a verifier can set any threshold and accept loa >= it.

lids.description: Linked identifiers the vetter was able to use as references for this legal entity. At least one should be globally unambiguous and portable across jurisdictions (e.g. an LEI); others may come from national registries, OpenCorporates, EDGAR, Dun & Bradstreet, a stock exchange, a social media handle, or a domain name. The kind of each item is detectable by regex match rather than declared.

issuer.description: Edge to a credential that establishes who the vetting issuer is

n.description: SAID of a credential that proves the identity of the issuer

s.description: SAID of the schema of the credential this edge points to

o.description: Operator: the issuer AID of this ACDC MUST be the issuee AID of the node this edge points to

oneOf.const: The level of assurance states which verification procedures the issuer carried out. It is not a guarantee about the organization, and it transfers no risk to the issuer beyond having performed those procedures. A verifier decides what level satisfies it and accepts loa at or above that threshold.

l.const: The level of assurance states which verification procedures the issuer carried out. It is not a guarantee about the organization, and it transfers no risk to the issuer beyond having performed those procedures. A verifier decides what level satisfies it and accepts loa at or above that threshold.

oneOf.const: Each tier asserts only what its own procedures establish. In particular, a credential below the tier that checks a thing says nothing about the organization's legal standing, signing authority, governance, tooling, solvency or competence, and a verifier MUST NOT infer any of them from the organization having been vetted at all.

oneOf.const: The linked identifiers are the references the vetter was able to use. The issuer does not assert that each registry entry is current, accurate, or exclusively controlled by this organization, and a verifier that relies on one MUST check it at its source.

l.const: The linked identifiers are the references the vetter was able to use. The issuer does not assert that each registry entry is current, accurate, or exclusively controlled by this organization, and a verifier that relies on one MUST check it at its source.

oneOf.const: The vetting speaks as of its stated datetime. The issuer agrees to revoke promptly once it believes the tier no longer holds, and a verifier MUST check the registry rather than treat an unexpired credential as current.
